name: ProTIP: Progressive Tool Retrieval Improves Planning
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2312.10332, cs.IR; cs.AI; cs.LG); not peer-reviewed at time of posting
authors_affiliation: Raviteja Anantha, Bortik Bandyopadhyay (equal contribution), Anirudh Kashi, Sayantan Mahinder, Andrew W Hill, Srinivas Chappidi -- all at Apple.
code_url: N/A (no official code release found; Apple ML research landing page exists at https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/pro-tip, but no public code repository)
task_domain: tool-use / multi-step planning (LLM agent that selects APIs/tools from an external toolbox to fulfill complex multi-step requests).
problem_setting: Offline, single-agent setting on the ToolBench dataset. The goal is to retrieve the correct top-k tools for a complex multi-step query and then generate a step-by-step plan (next-API prediction) with a fine-tuned LLM planner. Supervision is available: each request has ground-truth tool and plan labels. The work decouples Tool Retrieval (TR) evaluation from progressive planning. It explicitly notes that true end-to-end interactive step-by-step planning (executing each predicted API and feeding its output back) is deferred to future work; experiments use a tool-interleaving strategy rather than live execution.
what_is_retrieved: tools / APIs (specifically tool descriptions from an external toolbox).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus -- a fixed toolbox of ~16,000 tool descriptions indexed in a vector database; no agent-written growing memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Recovery of the complete minimal set of tools needed across all subtasks of a multi-step query, measured via Recall@K (K from 6 to 20). Retrieval is progressive/iterative per subtask, with the union (interleaving) of per-step retrieved tools forming the top-K set; objective is completeness over the multi-tool plan rather than a single fixed top-k ranking.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False -- the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is a contrastive-learning embedding retrieval method.
retrieval_unit: tool-API (a single tool, represented by its tool description / name + description). Retrieval is performed one tool per planning subtask.
index_source: Static corpus: the ToolBench toolbox (16,000 tools, 49 categories) is encoded offline into a vector database of tool-description embeddings; the store is frozen, not grown at test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat vector index (vector database of tool-description embeddings); cosine/L2 similarity over a flat embedding space. No graph or hierarchical organization of the index itself.
retriever_type: Dense / learned: a fine-tuned BERT-base-uncased bi-encoder for ProTIP. Baselines include BM25 (text-based) and GTR-T5-XL dense semantic search (off-the-shelf).
retriever_learning_signal: Contrastive learning on similarity labels: margin-based contrastive loss (Hadsell et al. 2006), margin m=0.3, L2 distance. Positive pairs = (progressively transformed query embedding, ground-truth next-tool description); negatives = randomly drawn irrelevant tools (in-batch). The query embedding for step i>1 is formed by element-wise subtracting embeddings of previously retrieved tool descriptions from the full-query embedding, so the retriever implicitly learns task decomposition without explicit subtask labels.
query_construction: Progressive/iterative query transformation in vector space: initial retrieval uses E_w(q) (the full-query embedding); for subsequent steps the query key is E_w(q) minus the element-wise sum of embeddings of previously retrieved tool descriptions, approximating an embedding for the remaining (i+1..n) subtasks. No explicit text decomposition is generated.
query_granularity: Step/subtask-level: a distinct query embedding is constructed per planning step (conditioned on execution history), in contrast to single-step full-query retrieval or explicit task-decomposition into text subqueries.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative -- retrieval is performed progressively, once per subtask/planning step, up to the number of subtasks in the query (max 6 in ToolBench).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule tied to the multi-step plan structure: one retrieval per subtask step, iterating until the subtasks are exhausted (the number of steps is bounded by the plan length / top-k budget). Not uncertainty- or confidence-triggered.
reranking: No dedicated reranking stage. Final top-K is assembled via a tool-interleaving strategy that merges per-step (per-subtask) retrieved tools into the final candidate set for Recall@K evaluation.
retrieved_context_refinement: Interleaving of per-subtask retrieved tools to form the final top-K set; otherwise no explicit distillation/compression/distractor-filtering of retrieved tool descriptions (the embedding-subtraction operation that removes already-addressed subtasks happens on the query side, not on retrieved context).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation for planning: the retrieved top-k tool candidates (with metadata, e.g., tool name) are inserted into the LLM planner's prompt (alongside the instruction, the request, and optional execution history) so the planner selects the next API to execute. Retrieval itself is also a learned-embedding signal (contrastive fine-tuning).
planning_integration: Per-step interleaved retrieve-then-plan: tools are retrieved progressively per subtask and supplied to a supervised fine-tuned LLM planner (OpenLLaMA-7B-v2) that predicts the next API per step. Note the authors evaluate planning by unrolling each interaction into per-step prompts and use tool interleaving for candidate sets rather than a fully live execution loop (true end-to-end step-by-step execution is deferred to future work).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-tool-call / per-subtask step: retrieval is woven in once per plan step (next-API prediction), not per CoT token or per sentence.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw tool metadata injected as text into the planner prompt -- primarily the tool name (and optionally tool description/metadata); the planner selects from this candidate list. On the retrieval side the unit is a tool-description embedding.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single tool/API specification (tool name + description) -- a concrete actionable unit, not a distilled strategy, workflow, or trajectory.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Contrastive/retriever-aware training: ProTIP is fine-tuned with negatives, and the planner is trained with (K-p) randomly sampled distractor tools added to the p ground-truth tools per step so it learns to pick the correct tool amid distractors. The paper discusses (as a limitation) that random-distractor training versus semantically-similar test-time distractors causes a train/test mismatch and proposes using TR-retrieved tools during training as future work. No explicit relevance-evaluator or self-reflection module.
memory_type: none (static toolbox index; no episodic/skill/workflow memory).
write_back: False -- the system does not write new experiences, cases, or skills into a memory store; the toolbox index is fixed.
online_growth: False -- the retrievable store (toolbox) is frozen after offline encoding and does not grow during deployment/test-time.
failure_experience_usage: Success-only with respect to retrieval supervision (positive = ground-truth next tool; negatives are randomly sampled irrelevant tools used contrastively, not stored failed trajectories). No storage/retrieval of failed execution experiences.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate; index is append-only at construction and otherwise static).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Partially: retrieval is a learned dense embedding model (contrastive fine-tuning that implicitly performs task decomposition) rather than off-the-shelf top-k similarity, but it is NOT an RL-optimized or value-based selection policy -- selection is still nearest-neighbor in the learned (progressively transformed) embedding space.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A -- single-agent, single-framework; no cross-agent memory or experience sharing.
benchmarks: ToolBench (Qin et al. 2023b). 16,000 tools across 49 categories, ~27,000 complex requests; after cleaning (removing hallucinated/invalid-tool annotations) ~25,489 train / 274 test requests, and after TD-outlier filtering 25,124 train / 268 test data points. Max subtasks per query = 6; avg ~2.93 subtasks.
baselines: Full-query BM25; Task-Decomposition (TD, via ChatGPT) BM25 with tool interleaving; Full-query Semantic Search (SS) with GTR-T5-XL; TD-based Semantic Search with tool interleaving; Oracle TR (ground-truth tools, plus a variant with GT + random tools). Planner backbone: supervised fine-tuned OpenLLaMA-7B-v2.
key_metrics: Tool Retrieval: Recall@K (K=6,10,15,20). Planning: Tool Accuracy (TA, %), Tool Hallucination (TH, %), Exact Match (EM), ROUGE-LSum (RLSum).
headline_result: On ToolBench, ProTIP outperforms the ChatGPT task-decomposition-based TR approach by ~24% in Recall@K=10 (ProTIP 81.36 vs TD-based Semantic Search 65.57, i.e. ~15.79 absolute points) and yields ~41% enhancement in Tool Accuracy for plan generation (ProTIP planner setting [T+H] TA=36.49% vs TD-based SS [T+H] TA=25.88%).
ablations: Reported as comparative settings rather than a single ablation table. (1) TR ablation across retrievers: full-query BM25 < TD-BM25 < full-query SS < TD-SS < ProTIP (Recall@10: 41 / 47 / 60.86 / 65.57 / 81.36). (2) Prompt-content ablation for the planner: tools-only [T] vs tools+history [T+H] -- adding execution history gives large TA gains (PTR [T] 19.82% -> [T+H] 36.49%, ~80%+ relative; Oracle-GT [T] 46.59% -> [T+H] 80.3%, ~70%+ relative), at the cost of higher Tool Hallucination and truncation risk. (3) Oracle upper bounds: GT+random tools vs only-GT tools (TA 77.53% vs 80.3% at [T+H]), quantifying headroom of TR-based planners vs oracle retrieval. The Recall@K of the retriever correlates with downstream Tool Accuracy (BM25 < SS < PTR).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes -- intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@K, Table 1) are reported separately from end-to-end planning metrics (TA/TH/EM/RLSum, Table 2), and the paper explicitly correlates retrieval recall with downstream tool accuracy.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both, partially: outcome-style plan metrics (EM, ROUGE-LSum over full predicted output incl. parameters) plus process-oriented per-step tool-selection quality (Tool Accuracy, Tool Hallucination) and step-wise retrieval Recall@K. Planning is evaluated on unrolled per-step prompts rather than a fully executed end-to-end trajectory.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: ProTIP is positioned as lightweight: a fine-tuned BERT-base-uncased bi-encoder that avoids expensive LLM (ChatGPT) task decomposition at inference, while outperforming the LLM-augmented TD baseline. Planner fine-tuning is resource-heavy: each configuration needs 8 A100 GPUs on AWS; context window 2048 tokens; ~12.3% of train and ~12.25% of test inputs exceed 2048 tokens causing truncation. No explicit latency/API-cost numbers reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Planner context window = 2048 tokens. Top-k fixed at K=10 (chosen to balance the 2048-token budget against max plan length p<=6), with p ground-truth tools plus (K-p) random/retrieved tools per step during training; Recall@K reported for K=6,10,15,20. Inputs exceeding 2048 tokens are truncated.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Uses (does not construct) ToolBench: an LLM(ChatGPT)-synthesized instruction-tuning dataset, 16,000 tools / 49 categories / ~27,000 requests, with tool and plan labels. The authors note ToolBench is susceptible to hallucinated tool annotations and perform cleaning (removing imaginary-tool requests, manual correction), yielding ~25,124 train / 268 test points. Best-system (Oracle, only-GT, [T+H]) Tool Accuracy ~80.3%, signaling substantial difficulty for TR-based planners (best non-oracle TA 36.49%).
how_retrieved_used_note: Retrieved tools are placed in the LLM planner prompt for per-step API selection; ProTIP's embedding transformation conditions retrieval on execution history.
builds_on: Word/embedding-space arithmetic and analogy regularities (Mikolov et al. 2013; Pennington et al. 2014 GloVe; Levy & Goldberg 2014); contrastive loss for metric learning (Hadsell et al. 2006); dense dual-encoder retrieval GTR-T5-XL (Ni et al. 2021) and BM25 (Robertson et al. 1995); BERT-base-uncased encoder; ToolBench / ToolLLM (Qin et al. 2023b); OpenLLaMA-7B-v2 (Geng & Liu 2023 / LLaMA Touvron et al. 2023) planner; Retrieval-Augmented Generation (Lewis et al. 2021); Decomposed Prompting (Khot et al. 2022).
contrasts_with: Single-step full-query tool retrieval (cannot model inter-tool dependency) and explicit task-decomposition (TD) retrieval -- in particular ChatGPT-based TD (requires subtask-tool atomicity alignment, costly LLM rewrites, operates in text space susceptible to OOV/semantic issues). Also contrasts with Gorilla (Patil et al. 2023) and ToolLLM/ToolBench retrieval as standard tool-retrieval baselines.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). Early (Dec 2023) step-wise / progressive tool-retrieval method: introduces per-subtask progressive tool retrieval via contrastive embedding-space query transformation, sitting in the lineage between single-step and explicit-task-decomposition tool retrieval, and a precursor to later tool-dependency-aware and graph-based tool-retrieval work.
tool_document_engineering: Tool descriptions are used largely as-is (raw tool name + description encoded by BERT-base for ProTIP, GTR-T5-XL for SS, or BM25 over description text). No synthetic-query augmentation or expanded summaries; the paper notes (as future work) that enriching tool metadata could improve generalization to unseen tools.
index_content_separation: No explicit lightweight-index-then-content (progressive-disclosure) separation; tool-description embeddings are the index and the retrieved tool metadata is loaded into the prompt directly. (Top-k truncation to fit the 2048-token budget is a budget mechanism, not index/content separation.)
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index (frozen ToolBench toolbox); no live synchronization, RapidAPI/MCP/RESTful auto-sync, or CRUD updates implemented. The motivation mentions toolboxes can evolve dynamically (creating subtask-tool atomicity-alignment problems), which ProTIP's implicit-TD design aims to be robust to, but the evaluated index itself is static.
tool_dependency_awareness: Yes (implicitly): a primary motivation is handling 'inter-tool dependency' across multi-step plans. ProTIP conditions each retrieval step on execution history by subtracting previously retrieved tool-description embeddings, so the next-tool retrieval depends on prior tool selections. However, dependencies are modeled implicitly in embedding space, not via an explicit dependency graph or bipartite KG.
